title: The King, O Lord, with Songs of Praise
description: The King, O Lord, with Songs of Praise in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 21, part 1, headed “Our king is the care of heaven”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The king, O Lord, with songs of praise, Shall in thy strength re-joice; And, blest with thy sal-va-tion, raise To heaven his cheer-ful voice.

lines: The king, O Lord, with songs of praise,
And, blest with thy salvation, raise
Thy sure defence, thro' nations round,
Then let the king on God alone
His mercy shall support the throne,
But, righteous Lord, his stubborn foes
Thy vengeful arm shall find out those
When thou against them dost engage,
Shall, like a fiery oven's rage,
Thus, Lord, thy wondrous power declare,
Whilst we glad songs of praise prepare

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
